title: INFORMATION OVERLOAD: How social media and AI can push you to the edge of insanity
description: Send us Fan Mail Is AI the modern-day puppet master pulling the strings of misinformation? Join Jimmy Rhodes and Matt Cartwright, as they untangle the web of trust and deception in the post-truth era and explore the effects of information overload on Matt's mental health. Triggered by a tragic incident in Southport, UK, we investigate how false information can ignite societal unrest and how AI-generated content like deep fakes intensifies disinformation. How do you find the truth in an ocean of conflicting information? And who decides what the truth is anyway? We delve into the overwhelming flood of data in our digital age, examining the evolving nature of scientific inquiry through debates like the origins of COVID-19. We also explore the role of spirituality as a potential anchor in chaotic times. As social media algorithms deepen echo chambers and terms like "conspiracy theory" are wielded to silence dissent, we stress the necessity of keeping an open mind and questioning our assumptions to foster a healthier relationship with the media landscape. Is free speech a double-edged sword in the age of information overload? We navigate the delicate balance between freedom of expression and the dangers of unregulated content, drawing from personal experiences with social media addiction and the need to distinguish entertainment from education. We explore theories about global cabals, 5G and iodised salt, discuss the potential influence of hostile states on misinformation and emphasize critical thinking and evidence-based analysis. Our discussion underscores the importance of reconnecting with offline reality to maintain mental well-being in a world increasingly dominated by digital narratives. Join us for a compelling exploration of trust, truth, and technology. (1) Exclusive: UK Gov Sneaks Ingredient Into Food Supply (substack.com)
summary: Triggered by the UK riots after the Southport stabbings, the hosts take on disinformation and information overload — with Matt bravely monologuing about his own 18-month spiral through hundreds of COVID, vaccine and cabal theories. Jimmy preaches epistemic humility and curated information diets, while both admit they no longer know what to believe, and an AI-generated rap battle provides light relief.
keyTalkingPoints: Matt opens up about months of consuming conspiracy content: he realised he simply cannot know what is true, and the overload itself — not any single theory — was the damage
AI supercharges the problem: anyone will soon generate convincing video, images and voice of anyone saying anything, with no verification solution yet
Research suggested roughly 10-15% of internet data is AI or bot-farm generated and 30% of traffic is bots — 50% is not far off
Jimmy's method: treat everything written online by strangers as fiction, curate sources, and know the limits of your own knowledge
The episode deliberately avoids adjudicating any theory, instead asking how normal people can function when narrative control is contested

jimmy: AI-generated deepfakes will be a huge, unsolved problem for elections and democracy
Treat everything written on the internet by someone you do not know as fiction
Freedom of speech beats narrative control — regulation just swaps one controller for another
He has largely opted out: no Twitter or Facebook, curated YouTube, and theories taken with a pinch of salt
matt: He is no longer sure he can ever know what is true — the sheer volume of contradictory information defeated him
Narrative control by platforms and media frightens him more than any individual theory
Both sides now present everything as irrefutable fact and neither wants debate
Social media addiction is underplayed and has literally rewired how brains consume information
